findings.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — [P1, confidence 100] "def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})" Trigger: any caller uses the pre-existing `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` contract; consequence: Ruby replaces the line-145 definition with this one and the five-argument call is rejected before transformation (wrong-shape and simplification advisory: one method must normalize both accepted shapes or the new operation must have a distinct name; the strongest counterargument that both definitions preserve compatibility fails because Ruby does not overload methods by arity).

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — [P1, confidence 100] "var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB" Trigger: validating an attachment on a site whose `max_attachment_size_kb` differs from 10 MB; consequence: the browser rejects server-valid attachments above 10 MB and submits server-invalid attachments below 10 MB (coupling advisory: upload policy must remain type-specific and server-owned; the strongest counterargument that 10 MB is the new pre-downsize ingress ceiling fails because attachments are never downsized).

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — [P2, confidence 100] "tempfile = FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, \"discourse-upload-#{type}\") rescue nil" Trigger: an API URL image is larger than 10 MB while `max_image_size_kb` is configured above 10 MB; consequence: this new literal rejects an upload that the configured policy and previous implementation accept (coupling advisory: a separate preprocessing ingress limit needs one explicit server setting shared with clients; the strongest counterargument that the literal is an intentional operational ceiling fails because it silently supersedes the existing configurable contract only on this ingestion path).

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — [P2, confidence 100] "while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes" Trigger: an image remains above the configured byte limit after five 80%-dimension transforms; consequence: the loop terminates and passes an image that violates its promised size invariant into `Upload.create_for` (wrong-shape and deletion advisory: a single upload-preprocessing owner must produce or reject against the target-byte postcondition instead of embedding a five-pass geometry heuristic in the controller; the strongest counterargument that five attempts safely bounds work fails because that bound explicitly permits the oversized terminal state while still performing up to five full image rewrites).

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — [P2, confidence 100] "var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB" When max_image_size_kb or max_attachment_size_kb exceeds 10240, a file between 10 MB and its configured allowance is rejected before upload, so this image feature also regresses valid configured image and attachment uploads.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — [P2, confidence 100] "while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes" When an image remains above the configured limit after the fifth 80% reduction, this loop exits without satisfying the filesize postcondition and hands an over-limit image to the normal upload path instead of automatically downsizing it.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — [P3, confidence 100] "if tempfile && tempfile.size > 0 && SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0 && FileHelper.is_image?(filename)" The diff adds no automated coverage for configured thresholds, retry exhaustion, or animated-image handling, leaving CI unable to verify the feature's acceptance boundaries (advisory: the strongest counterargument that the branch is simple fails because its outcome depends on mutable settings and external image-format behavior).

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — [P1, confidence 100] "def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})" Ruby replaces the five-positional-argument `downsize` definition at line 145 with this definition, so every existing `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` invocation triggers `ArgumentError` before ImageMagick runs.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — [P2, confidence 100] "var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB" When `type` is `attachment` and `max_attachment_size_kb` is above 10240, this unconditional client limit rejects a server-permitted attachment before upload, making the configured large-attachment path impossible to execute.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — [P2, confidence 75] "tempfile = FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, \"discourse-upload-#{type}\") rescue nil" When an API URL names an image between 10 MB and a configured `max_image_size_kb` above 10240, this reduced download ceiling yields `nil` and the later `tempfile.size` dereference raises instead of executing the formerly permitted upload.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — [P1, confidence 100] "var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB" When `max_image_size_kb` is configured above 10240, this fixed threshold rejects otherwise permitted images before the new downsizing path runs, so the change replaces the administrator's image-upload policy instead of preserving it while adding automatic downsizing.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — [P1, confidence 100] "tempfile = FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, \"discourse-upload-#{type}\") rescue nil" Trigger: an API URL download is rejected at the new 10 MB ceiling; consequence: the rescue changes the failure to `nil`, line 72 dereferences `tempfile.size`, synchronous callers receive a raw 500, and deferred callers have already received success but never receive a MessageBus outcome.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — [P1, confidence 100] "OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, \"80%\", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)" Trigger: ImageMagick does not exit while processing an oversized image; consequence: this request-path subprocess has no timeout, so a synchronous upload never returns and a deferred upload has already reported success while its worker remains occupied and publishes no result.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — [P1, confidence 100] "OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, \"80%\", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)" Trigger: an oversized animated GIF is held in a tempfile path that does not end in `.GIF`; consequence: animation dispatch tests that tempfile path, selects the non-animated `from[0]` conversion, and reports a successful upload after silently dropping every frame except the first.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — [P1, confidence 100] "OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, \"80%\", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)" An authenticated API request with a shell-metacharacter-bearing `type` (for example `image;id;#`) and an oversized image URL causes `FileHelper.download` to preserve that value in the tempfile path and this new call to pass the path into `convert_with`'s shell interpolation, executing attacker-selected OS commands as the application user before upload validation.

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — [P2, confidence 100] "var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10 MB" Trigger: an upstream server configured with a body cap below 10 MB returns 413; consequence: the UI falsely tells the user that 10 MB is allowed, so retries within the displayed limit deterministically fail again.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the hardcoded value '10 * 1024' (10 MB) replaces the dynamic SiteSetting lookup for maxSizeKB in the 413 error handler. The finding correctly identifies that if an upstream server (like nginx) is configured with a body size limit below 10 MB, it will return 413, but the UI will display '10 MB' as the limit. This creates a misleading error message where users are told they can upload up to 10 MB when the actual limit is lower, causing repeated failures. This is a real defect introduced by the hardcoded value replacing the configurable setting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — [P1, confidence 100] "var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB" Triggering validation for a non-image attachment now replaces the configured `max_attachment_size_kb` policy with this image-ingest ceiling, so sites configured above 10 MB reject valid attachments and sites configured below 10 MB submit attachments that the server rejects.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that line 182 in utilities.js changes from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024`. This function handles validation for different file types (the 'type' parameter determines whether it's an image or attachment). By hardcoding 10MB, the code no longer respects the site's configured `max_attachment_size_kb` setting for non-image uploads. Sites with attachment limits above 10MB would incorrectly reject valid attachments client-side, and sites with limits below 10MB would allow uploads that the server would then reject. This is a real bug affecting attachment upload validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — [P1, confidence 100] "OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, \"80%\", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)" An authenticated API request with a shell-metacharacter-bearing `type` (for example `image;id;#`) and an oversized image URL causes `FileHelper.download` to preserve that value in the tempfile path and this new call to pass the path into `convert_with`'s shell interpolation, executing attacker-selected OS commands as the application user before upload validation.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that the `type` parameter flows into the tempfile path and then into shell interpolation. However, examining the diff: (1) The tempfile is created by `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")` where `type` is used in the tempfile name prefix, not the path. Ruby's Tempfile creates files in a temp directory with sanitized names. (2) The `convert_with` method uses `instructions.join(" ")` with backticks, but the instructions come from `downsize_instructions` or `downsize_instructions_animated` methods (not shown in diff but referenced). The path passed is `tempfile.path` which is controlled by Ruby's Tempfile, not directly by user input. (3) The `type` parameter in the controller comes from `params[:type]` but there's no evidence it flows unsanitized into shell commands. The finding makes assumptions about code behavior not visible in the diff.
